name: command
title: Command
description: A command palette on a slip of paper. Type and the list is sorted and cut down (cmdk's fuzzy match); the row you are on wears the highlighter, keys show as pencil keycaps, an empty search gets Stubby with his magnifier. Put it in a dialog and it is set on a napkin.

a11y: cmdk: the input is a `role=combobox` with `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`; the list is a `role=listbox` of `role=option` rows with `aria-selected` and `aria-disabled`. Focus stays in the input; the arrow keys move the highlight, Home and End jump, Enter chooses, and `loop` wraps.
Ctrl + N / P / J / K also move the highlight (cmdk's vim bindings; `vimBindings={false}` turns them off).
A polite status under the search field says "3 results" or "No results" after each keystroke, which cmdk does not do by itself. The empty message is shown as well.
The highlighted row is a highlighter-yellow shape, not only a hue; a disabled row is graphite and dimmed but still readable.

CommandDialog is a Reka UI dialog: focus goes into the input and Escape closes. Reka UI returns focus only to a `DialogTrigger`; a palette opened by a shortcut or a button that sets `open` has none, so CommandDialog remembers who had the focus when it opened and gives it back when it closes, unless the app has moved it on by then (choose a result, go to that page, and the focus stays on the new page's heading instead of jumping back to the button). Its title and description are `sr-only`.

The input's `aria-activedescendant` always names the selected row: cmdk records it before it has redrawn the rows, so after typing it could name a row that was gone; `CommandInput` corrects it after every keystroke. If you render cmdk's `Command.Input` yourself inside a `Command`, call `useFreshActiveDescendant(inputRef)` from this file.
Reduced motion: no drop-in or zoom, and no loop animation in Loading. Forced colors: the rule under the field becomes a real border and the highlighted row gets a Highlight background.
meta.usage:
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandShortcut } from "@/components/ui/command"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Command class="w-80">
      <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search..." />
      <CommandList>
        <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
        <CommandGroup heading="Suggestions">
          <CommandItem>Calendar</CommandItem>
          <CommandItem>
            Settings
            <CommandShortcut>Ctrl S</CommandShortcut>
          </CommandItem>
        </CommandGroup>
      </CommandList>
    </Command>
  )
}
